recipe: Sesame-peanut noodles with crisp chilli tofu crumble
servesNote: 2 portions — 909 kcal / 54 g protein each, VEGAN. ⭐ The only dish in the set eaten at room temperature, which makes it the best of all of them for Maria's next-day lunch: cold sesame noodles are supposed to be cold.
adaptations: ⛔ THE TOASTED SESAME OIL IS OUT, and in this dish that is not a small thing. The whole justification for using peanut butter instead of sesame paste is that the sesame-oil sachet puts back the toasted aroma peanut butter lacks. Without it this becomes a peanut noodle bowl — still good, but it is a different dish, and no amount of extra peanut butter substitutes.

⛔ THE GINGER & GARLIC PASTE IS OUT TOO. Use a thumb of fresh ginger grated with an extra clove of garlic if you have ginger; if not, lean on the fresh garlic the recipe already calls for and accept a flatter sauce.

⚠️ SOY IS DOWN TO 4 SACHETS AND THERE IS NO BOTTLE — three Shoda 8 g and one Gousto 30 ml, about 54 ml in total. This recipe wants 40 ml, so it takes most of what is left. ⛔ The 8 g sachets will not cover the 25 ml the sauce needs on their own; the 30 ml sachet has to go into the sauce and the small ones onto the tofu.

⚠️ DRIED PASTA IS 'VERY LITTLE' and this wants 150 g of spaghetti. Tuesday bought fusilli and tagliatelle — neither is right for a noodle bowl, but fusilli will hold the sauce if it comes to it. Check the packet before you start.
⛔ THE TOFU IS NOT IN THE HOUSE — 540 g, three blocks, and it is the load-bearing decision. Two blocks drops this to 42 g protein a portion and it stops qualifying for the slot.

prep: Drain the tofu and pat all three blocks thoroughly dry. Super-firm needs no pressing — that is the whole point of buying it — but surface water will steam rather than fry.
⭐ Crumble the tofu with your fingers, from coarse-breadcrumb size up to small peas. Uneven is good: the small bits go crisp, the bigger bits stay chewy, and you want both.

Slice the spring onions on the diagonal and keep the whites and greens in separate piles — the whites go into the hot chilli oil, the greens go raw on top at the end. Grate the garlic. Cut the cucumber into matchsticks.

steps.text: Large frying pan, medium-high, ⛔ NO OIL AT ALL. Tofu in. Dry-fry, stirring occasionally, until the pan stops hissing with steam and the crumbs start to squeak and colour. ⭐ Driving the water off before any fat goes in is what makes the difference — oil added too early just seals the moisture in.
NOW 10 ml oil, the chilli powder, smoked paprika and a good pinch of salt, frying and stirring more often, until the crumbs are browned at the edges and rattle loosely in the pan.

Pour in 15 ml soy and the rice wine and stir hard. It will hiss and steam — the liquid seasons the crumble and lifts all the browned residue off the base into it. Cook until the pan is dry again and the crumbs are glossy and dark. Onto a plate, spread out rather than heaped, or it steams itself soft. Wipe the pan.

Chilli oil. Spring onion whites and half the grated garlic in a small heatproof bowl with 1 tsp chilli powder. Heat the remaining 10 ml oil until it shimmers and just begins to move quickly — NOT smoking — then pour it over. It should sizzle immediately and smell nutty. ⚠️ Burnt chilli is bitter and unfixable, so err cool.

⭐ THE SAUCE, IN THE RIGHT ORDER. Peanut butter in a bowl. Warm water ONE TABLESPOON AT A TIME, stirring smooth after each addition. It will get THICKER and claggier before it gets thinner — this is normal and is the step everyone gets wrong. Keep going, ~3–4 tbsp, until it loosens to the consistency of double cream.

Into that: 25 ml soy, the vinegar, the sesame oil, the ginger & garlic paste, 2 sriracha, honey, the remaining garlic and black pepper. Then the chilli oil from the last step, aromatics and all. Taste it NOW — salty, nutty, sour and sweet in that order, and slightly too strong on its own, because the noodles will dilute it. Flat? Almost always short of vinegar or salt.

⭐ Divide the sauce between two wide bowls, spooning it into the BOTTOM. Sauce underneath and noodles on top is the standard Sichuan noodle-bowl assembly — it means the sauce is tossed up from the base at the table rather than sitting on top going gluey.

Spaghetti in well-salted water until just PAST al dente — a shade softer than you would want for an Italian sauce, because it firms up when rinsed. ⭐ Save a cupful of the cooking water before draining.

⛔ Drain and IMMEDIATELY rinse under cold running water, moving them with your hand until they feel cool and no longer slippery. This washes off the surface starch. Skip it and the noodles glue themselves into a single mass and the sauce slides off. Shake very dry.

Noodles onto the sauce. A tablespoon or two of the reserved HOT cooking water per bowl, and toss thoroughly FROM THE BOTTOM UP until every strand is coated and the sauce has gone from paste to a clinging dressing.

Top with the tofu crumble, cucumber and spring onion greens. ⭐ Serve at room temperature or barely warm — this dish is actively worse piping hot, because heat thins the sesame sauce and dulls the vinegar. Maria's next-day lunch: store the noodles-in-sauce and the crumble in separate containers, eat straight from the fridge, ⛔ do not microwave, and stir a tablespoon of hot water through first — the sauce tightens overnight.
